headline:
Human-triggered avalanches are possible in alpine terrain.
Rogers Pass is experiencing a record-low snowpack, with insufficient coverage for safe ski and snowboard travel across much of the region.
Early-season hazards remain widespread, including buried rocks, stumps, and logs.
snowpack:
40cm of warm, heavy snow at treeline and in the alpine in the last 72hrs. Moderate to strong SW winds redistributed this snow loading lee features in exposed terrain.
Storm snow covers a record low snowpack consisting of crusts and facets. Buried wind slabs exist at ridgetop and in cross loaded areas in the Alpine. HS at treeline is ~ 65 cm, with ~10 cm at trailhead.
detail:
Wednesday afternoon into Thursday a cycle of natural avalanches occurred in the steep, gully features east of Rogers Pass. Natural avalanches up to size 3 were observed, terminating on the fans.
As natural avalanches taper off into the weekend, human triggered avalanches are still possible.

region: Weißkugel Group, Stubai Alps Central, Zillertal Alps Northwest
headline: Weak layers in the old snowpack necessitate caution. Fresh wind slabs require caution.
snowpack:
Avalanche prone weak layers exist in the old snowpack. This applies in particular on west, north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m, as well as in all aspects above approximately 3000 m. Avalanches triggered by explosives and whumpfing sounds and the formation of shooting cracks when stepping on the snowpack confirm the unfavourable bonding of the snowpack. 
 In many areas 15 to 20 cm of snow fell on Thursday,, and locally up to 30 cm. The wind has transported the new snow. This applies in particular at high altitudes and in high Alpine regions. The fresh wind slabs are lying on soft layers. 
 As a consequence of warming during the day and solar radiation more frequent mostly small loose snow avalanches are to be expected. This applies on extremely steep sunny slopes.
detail:
Weak layers in the lower part of the snowpack can be released even by individual winter sport participants. This applies on steep west, north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m, as well as in all aspects above approximately 3000 m. Remotely triggered avalanches are possible in isolated cases. This applies in high Alpine regions. Mostly avalanches are medium-sized. 
 In addition the fresh wind slabs should be taken into account. Such avalanche prone locations are to be found in steep terrain above approximately 2400 m. Caution is to be exercised adjacent to ridgelines, as well as in gullies and bowls, and behind abrupt changes in the terrain. The number and size of avalanche prone locations will increase with altitude. Avalanches can reach medium size. 
 The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
trend: The avalanche danger will persist. Experience in the assessment of avalanche danger is required.

headline:
The snowpack remains too shallow to avalanche in most areas.
Avalanche hazard is isolated to steep, smooth slopes at higher elevations.
snowpack:
Up to 30 cm of recent snow at upper elevations has added to a shallow early-season snowpack.
A widespread melt-freeze crust exists 10 to 20 cm off the ground. Weak faceted snow has likely formed around the crust in many places.
Snow depths taper rapidly at lower elevations.
With the shallow snow and exposed ground roughness, avalanches are unlikely across most terrain. However, small avalanches are possible on steep, open slopes lacking anchoring features like exposed rocks and vegetation.
detail:
No recent avalanches have been reported, likely because the shallow snowpack remains largely below the threshold to slide.
As new snow continues to accumulate, expect more terrain to become deep enough to avalanche.

headline:
Avalanche danger will increase throughout the day Saturday as strong winds drift new snow at upper elevations. You can trigger an avalanche where winds drift new snow into thicker and more connected slabs on lee slopes. The most dangerous slopes face north, northeast, and east, where new snow drifts onto a connected layer of weak old grains.
Choose wind-sheltered terrain for safer travel options.
Instabilités en altitude dans la neige restée froide et légère. Humidification du manteau neigeux en moyenne montagne.
snowpack:
Enneigement : 
Pour la saison, l’enneigement est excédentaire à toutes altitudes. On peut chausser les skis au-dessus de 1400 m. Peu de neige à cette altitude mais l'épaisseur augmente vite en montant en altitude. 
Les crêtes peuvent être décapées avec le fort vent des derniers épisodes. 
Présence de grosses corniches et congères. 
Qualité de la neige ce samedi :
* Sous 1900 m en nord et 2100 m en sud : La neige est alourdie en surface mais reste fraîche en dessous, ce qui donne un aspect assez dense. Croute de regel non portante le matin, puis la croute se ramolli rapidement avec l'arrivée du soleil. 
* Entre 1900 m et 2700 m : la neige est encore froide, poudreuse mais au fil de la journée, elle va s'alourdir en surface sous l'effet du redoux. Le manteau neigeux se tasse.
* Au-dessus de 2700 m : La neige est encore froide. Elle reste très légère dans la plupart des pentes. Toutefois, vers les crêtes/arêtes et au-dessus de 3000 m, la neige est parfois plus dure, travaillée par le vent.
detail:
Déclenchements provoqués :
* Au-dessus de 3000 m : plaques à vent. Elles se forment sous le fort vent de Nord-Ouest à Nord en journée de samedi, dans la neige restée légère. Plus nombreuses à proximité des crêtes et des arêtes. Taille 2 (moyenne), parfois 3 (grande). 
Observables : transport de neige par le vent, fissures sous les skis, irrégularités du manteau neigeux (accumulations/ablations)... 
Facteur aggravant : une couche fragile persistante est enfouie localement. Elle peut être sollicitée dans le cas d'une avalanche en cascade et engendrer une plus grande avalanche. 
* En dessous de 3000 m : une plaque à vent n'est pas exclue mais elles sont plus rares. Principalement dans les pentes qui restent à l'ombre. Taille 1 (petite) à 2 (moyenne).
* En dessous de 2700 m : de la neige humide peut couler sous les skis avec le réchauffement diurne. De plus en plus nombreux au fil de la journée et principalement en larges versants Sud dans les pentes raides. Taille 1 (petite) à 2 (moyenne). 
Départs spontanés :
* En dessous de 2700 m : départs en neige humide, notamment dans les pentes raides exposées au soleil et vers les rochers. Plus nombreux au fil du réchauffement diurne. Taille 1 (petite) à 2 (moyenne). 
* En dessous de 2500 m : plaques de fond. Possibles dans les pentes raides et lisses (pentes herbeuses, dalles rocheuses). Possibles à toute heure du jour et de la nuit, mais plus nombreuses au fil de la journée.

snowpack:
Snow depths are average for the time of year. Snow sports in open terrain are quite possible where the underlying ground is smooth. More recent wind slabs at elevated altitudes are in some cases still prone to triggering.
In addition, especially on shady slopes above approximately 2600 m, a weak layer of faceted, coarse-grained snow lies at the snow base. This weak layer is not yet overlain by much snow, so avalanches can be triggered by people in this layer.
